newsitem.title: USA: CFTC charges three over grain contracts.
newsitem.headline: CFTC charges three over grain contracts.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Wednesday it filed three administrative charges arising from grain contracts alleged to be in violation of federal commodities law.

The complaints were filed separately against Southern Thumb Co-op Inc, a cooperative grain elevator based in Lapeer, Mich., Grain Land Cooperative of Blue Earth, Minn., and Roger Wright of Mechanicsburg, Ohio, the CFTC said.
Southern is charged with violating the prohibition against the offer of illegal, off-exchange agricultural options and with fraud related to the marketing of the illegal contracts, the agency said.
Grain Land is accused of offering and entering into illegal, off-exchange futures contracts, it said.
The case against Robert Wright involves fraud related to his marketing and promotion of illegal, off-exchange futures and options contracts, it said.

Also charged in the Wright case is St. Louis-based brokerage firm A.G. Edwards Inc, Philip Luxenburger, an employee at the firm, and Buckeye Countrymark Inc, a Xenia, Ohio-based cooperative grain elevator, the agency said.

The broker and Luxenburger are charged with aiding and abetting Wright's alleged unregistered activities while Buckeye is accused of offering and entering into illegal, off-exchange futures and options contracts, CFTC said.
CFTC alleged that Grain Land Cooperative offered and sold so-called "hedge-to-arrive" contracts, which it said constituted illegal, off-exchange futures contracts.
The contracts blend aspects of traditional cash contracts and futures contracts, often allowing farmers to roll over the delivery date for grain.

CFTC enforment director Geoffrey Aronow said the commission decided to authorize filing of the cases "because it has reason to believe that the contracts marketed, offered and entered into ... are illegal off-exchange futures or options contracts."
